individual differences in language acquisition and processing are pervasive and that the nature of these differences is complex.
individual differences in language acquisition and processing are pervasive, systematic, and theoretically informative.
there is a great deal of variability in the way people learn and process language, that this variability is systematic, and that it is related to other aspects of cognition.

how individual differences in the acquisition and processing language are related to the architecture of the cognitive system and how these are related to individual differences in experience.

the study of ID in the domain of language is an important and growing area that is likely to provide significant insights into language processing and acquisition, and that the study of language processing and acquisition is an important and fruitful area in the study of ID.

there are individual differences in language processing and language acquisition.

the study of individual differences is a valuable source of evidence for the study of language and its acquisition and use, and that the field is ripe for the application of new and existing methods to the study of IDs in language.

there are substantial differences in how people acquire and process language, and that these differences are not random, but are instead systematic and lawful.
